text_blocks.snippet: In Utah, [Highlight start] asphalt shingles cost roughly half as much upfront and are a practical fit for shorter ownership timelines or lower budgets, while metal roofing lasts two to three times longer and handles mountain snow, high-altitude UV, and freeze-thaw cycles better [Highlight end] .

list.snippet: Asphalt Shingles: Typically cost $4.50–$8.00 per sq. ft. installed (around $12,500–$22,000 for an average ~2,500 sq. ft. roof, depending on impact rating). Expected lifespan in Utah is 20–30 years, often shortened by strong UV rays and freeze-thaw cycles.

Metal Roofing: Typically costs $7.00–$16.00+ per sq. ft. installed—often 1.5x to 3x the cost of asphalt depending on metal type and standing-seam vs. exposed-fastener panels. Expected lifespan is 40–70 years.

Snow & Ice: Metal sheds snow efficiently and helps reduce ice dams when paired with proper flashing and snow retention. Asphalt relies heavily on good attic ventilation and ice-and-water shield underlayment during heavy snow and melt cycles.

High-Altitude Sun & Temperature Swings: Intense UV at higher elevations (such as around Heber City and Park City) accelerates granule loss and drying on asphalt shingles. Quality coated metal resists UV breakdown and reflects more radiant heat.
Wind & Hail: Standing-seam metal and impact-rated systems handle high winds well, though severe hail can dent soft metal panels or bruise shingles depending on product rating.
Choose metal if you plan to stay long-term, want minimal replacement hassle, or own a higher-elevation/mountain home exposed to heavy snow and strong sun.
Choose asphalt shingles if you want the lowest upfront cost, plan to sell within several years, or need a roof that matches a traditional neighborhood look on a tighter budget.

list.snippet: How long you plan to stay in the home
Your approximate roof size and elevation (e.g., valley vs. mountain/Heber or Park City area)
Whether upfront budget or long-term durability matters most to you
